gen-dafont-dogica-gf-sen: Chunky, wide-spaced, and unapologetically loud. The strongest thing here is the gap in temperament: Dogica stamps wide, near-capital lowercase, while Sen traces tall letters in one constant line.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-stack-sans-notch: Dogica spreads its heavy letters out on very wide tracking, with lowercase that climbs nearly to capital height. Stack Sans Notch takes over with rod-like, uniform strokes and big, open curves.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-abeezee: Early GameBoy stretches its letters wide, with a skyward x-height. ABeeZee reads smoothly over many lines, its rounded strokes and open terminals keeping every word easy to follow.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-anek-devanag: Anek Devanagari keeps its letter mouths wide open. Down a full page, those openings and the tall middle zone keep text moving, while Early GameBoy stays out front with stretched spacing.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-anek-gujarat: Stretched-out and playful, right at the top. Anek Gujarati then reads comfortably for as long as you like, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals and its c gaping wide.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-blinker: Stretched and slightly scuffed, like worn charcoal. Early GameBoy commands attention with playful, widely spaced letters, while Blinker, plain sans all the way, keeps lines of constant thickness easy to take in.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-carrois-goth: Early GameBoy leads with wide, stretched spacing and a skyward x-height, built to command attention. And Carrois Gothic SC, plain sans at heart, handles the quiet work, with open curves and lowercase close to capital height.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-comme: Early GameBoy stretches its tracking wide and sends its x-height skyward, giving the heading a playful, commanding pull. Comme, a smooth sans-serif, settles in underneath with generous lowercase and clean curves.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-cossette-tex: Stretched, playful, and quietly commanding, Early GameBoy sets the tone with subtle thick-thin modulation. And Cossette Texte, plain sans with a wide-eyed e and a flat line weight, carries the text beneath it.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-fresca: Everything about the body text reads smoothly, with counters that open outward and no stroke turning heavy or light within a word. Fresca then picks up from Early GameBoy, whose stretched heading carries a worn-stamp restraint.
